name: Selenium WebDriver
summary: The W3C WebDriver reference implementation, with bindings for Java, Python, C#, JavaScript and Ruby and Selenium Grid for distributed runs.
strengths: W3C standard supported by every browser vendor.
The widest language support of any browser automation tool.
Selenium Grid and every cloud provider support it.
Copes well with legacy UIs, iframes and older browsers.
tradeoffs: No auto-waiting: you write explicit waits, a common source of flakiness.
No test runner, reporting or isolation built in; you assemble them yourself.
Slower and more verbose than modern alternatives for new projects.
